title: Show my user name and the groups I belong to
summary: Your user name is the account you are logged in as. Your groups decide what you may do, for example use sudo for administrator tasks or run Docker. Two read-only commands show both.

aliases.text: which user am I logged in as
am I in the sudo group
what groups does my user have
am I in the docker group
покажи мое имя пользователя и группы

steps.explain: Print the login name of the account you are using. Read-only: nothing is changed. If the output is root, you are in the superuser account.
steps.expect: Prints one word, your login name, for example tester.

steps.explain: Print the groups your account belongs to, on one line. Look for sudo or wheel on Linux (allows administrator commands with sudo), admin on macOS (administrator rights), and docker (allows running Docker without sudo).
steps.expect: Group names separated by spaces, for example: tester sudo. Your own group is usually in the list.

alternatives.explain: Print the user name, numeric IDs and all groups in one line. Use it when you also need the numbers, for example 1001 for your user.
alternatives.expect: For example: uid=1001(tester) gid=1001(tester) groups=1001(tester),27(sudo). The groups are listed after groups=.

alternatives.explain: Print only the group names of the current user, an older command that gives the same result as id -Gn.
alternatives.expect: Same group names as id -Gn, separated by spaces, for example: tester sudo.

source.title: id manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
